name: Phobos
tagline: The larger of Mars's two moons — a rubble-pile slowly spiraling toward its planet.
history: Phobos orbits Mars closer than any other moon in the Solar System orbits its planet — so near that it circles faster than Mars rotates, rising in the west and setting in the east twice each Martian day. Tidal forces are tearing it apart: it loses about 1.8 metres of altitude per century and will either crash into Mars or shred into a ring within 50 million years. Its battered surface, dominated by the 9-km Stickney crater, is covered in grooves whose origin is still debated. NASA's Mars Trek maps it in detail; the upcoming JAXA MMX mission will land there and return samples to Earth.
